claim: The claimants sought damages for the death of Khalid Mehmood due to the accident at the workplace.
requested_remedy: The claimants sought damages for the death of Khalid Mehmood due to the accident at the workplace.
parties: Plaintiff: BUSHRA BIBI AND NABELA QOSER, the co-administrators of the estate of KHALID, MEHMOOD, the deceased
Defendant: METHOD BUILDING & ENGINEERING WORKS LIMITED (in liquidation), LEIGHTON CONTRACTORS (ASIA) LIMITED and SAFEWELL GONDOLA (HK) LIMITED

facts.F1: The deceased was employed by the 1st defendant to carry out works in relation to the construction of certain aviation fuel facilities in Tuen Mun Area 38 in the New Territories.
facts.F2: The 2nd defendant was the principal contractor at the site and the 1st defendant was its sub-contractor in relation to some of the works being carried on at the site.
facts.F3: The 3rd defendant was responsible for the supply, installation and maintenance of suspended working platforms (gondolas) to be used for the work to be carried out.
facts.F4: On 2 July 2009, the project manager of the 1st defendant instructed the deceased and his team to remove rubbish, tools and other materials from inside Aviation Fuel Tank No. 5 and to carry out cleaning work inside the Tank.
facts.F5: The deceased and his co-workers started work and manually moved out safety harnesses, brushes, old cans and other items through the entrance.
facts.F6: A gondola that had been resting on the floor of the Tank was raised a certain distance from the ground so to enable cleaning work to be done on that part of the floor of the Tank that was immediately below the gondolas.
facts.F7: The deceased attempted to climb onto the working platform of the gondola but failed, and fell 22 metres and suffered multiple injuries from which he died.
facts.F8: The accident was reported and investigated by Mr. Chu Yan Chung, an Occupational Safety Officer of the Labour Department.
facts.F9: An inspection of gondola No. 2 revealed that the three-position control switch was stuck at the 'up' position and that the emergency stop button had not been activated.
facts.F10: The deceased faced a dilemma caused by the negligence of the 1st and 2nd defendants.
facts.F11: The deceased reacted to the dilemma by acting to protect the property of the 1st and 2nd defendants.
facts.F12: The deceased’s action was an ill-judged decision, taken on the spur of the moment, to safeguard the property of his employer, without properly appreciating the severity of the risk involved.

claim: a declaration as to possessory title arising out of the allegedly adverse possession of a residential flat in Ho Man Tin, Kowloon
requested_remedy: a declaration as to possessory title arising out of the allegedly adverse possession of a residential flat in Ho Man Tin, Kowloon

facts.F1: The Premises were purchased in 1972 by two gentlemen, Lai Yu (“Lai Senior”) and Poon Wing Chung (“Poon Senior”) as business partners.
facts.F2: The purchase was made jointly but for reasons that are immaterial, the decision was taken to register the property in the name of the defendant.
facts.F3: Lai Senior and Poon Senior’s business relationship turned sour and the partnership was dissolved in 1976.
facts.F4: After the dissolution of the partnership, Lai Senior seemed to have felt he was cheated by Poon Senior and treated Poon Senior’s share of the property as being his, in compensation.
facts.F5: The defendant had understood the property to be owned by him legally and beneficially since 1976.
facts.F6: There were no formal written agreements for the occupation of the Premises by Poon Senior’s brother, Poon Yiu Chung (“PYC”), or Poon Yiu Chung's family.
facts.F7: PYC’s occupation of the Premises initially as a tenancy at will, with a rental agreed, later became rent-free.
facts.F8: The plaintiff had been resident in the Premises since 1997 and had lived there rent-free throughout, the defendant contended that this occupation was with his permission.
facts.F9: The plaintiff changed the locks and the doors to the Premises after moving in in 1997.
facts.F10: The plaintiff has paid for the maintenance of the Premises and of the common parts of the building, and has paid utility and management charges.
facts.F11: The defendant has paid government rent and rates but has not visited or lived in the Premises during this period.
facts.F12: The first contact between the plaintiff and the defendant was when the defendant commenced proceedings to recover possession of the Premises.
facts.F13: The relationship between the parties suggested that the defendant would not seek independent physical entry to the Premises.
facts.F14: The plaintiff’s acts were insufficient to show an intention to possess the Premises exclusively and adverse to the paper owner.
facts.F15: The defendant knowingly acquiesced in the occupation of the Premises by the plaintiff and his family up to the commencement of the proceedings.

claim: damages for personal injuries suffered arising from a slip on a wet platform on 27 July 2002
requested_remedy: damages for personal injuries suffered arising from a slip on a wet platform on 27 July 2002

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was a general worker employed by Ever Success Garments Limited and was deployed to work at Room 508, Block B of the Office Tower at the Premises.
facts.F2: The Defendant was contractually responsible for maintaining the Premises, including all common areas and facilities.
facts.F3: On 27 July 2002, the Plaintiff slipped and fell on a wet platform while walking up the steps to the entrance of the Premises, resulting in a displaced fracture of the distal pole of her left patella.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff underwent emergency surgery, rehabilitation, and physiotherapy, but still suffered from residual pain, weakness, and stiffness in her left knee joint.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff claimed damages for personal injuries, pre-trial loss of earnings, future loss of earnings, loss of MPF contributions, loss of earning capacity, and special damages.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff had suffered significant residual pain, weakness, and stiffness in her left knee joint, which affected her employability and earning capacity.
